description: A single-panel double-logarithmic SAXS profile plot. The y-axis is labelled "Intensity (cm⁻¹)" with printed tick values -2, 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10; the x-axis is labelled "q (nm⁻¹)" with printed major tick labels 0.1, 1 and 10, the data spanning roughly 0.02 to 15 nm⁻¹. The legend lists Fe-5AL (open circles), Fe-6AL (open squares), Fe-6.8AL (open triangles), Fe-9AL (open diamonds) and a thick dark-navy line labelled "fits". Four red open-symbol data sets and four stacked fit curves are plotted; they have been offset vertically so that no absolute intensity comparison between compositions is possible, and the individual curves are not annotated with their composition. All four curves decrease monotonically with increasing q, appearing close to linear in this log-log presentation over low and mid q, and flattening or changing slope towards the high-q end. Thin red broken lines with dots run along the data. The figure argues that one fitted functional form reproduces the experimental SAXS curves of all four Fe-Al low-density steels and that scattering follows a q⁻⁴-type decay, which the caption assigns to the broken dotted lines.

subfigures.description: Double-logarithmic SAXS intensity (cm⁻¹) versus q (nm⁻¹) for four Fe-Al low-density steels (Fe-5AL circles, Fe-6AL squares, Fe-6.8AL triangles, Fe-9AL diamonds), each with open-symbol experimental data, a thick dark-navy fitted curve ('fits') and thin red broken dotted lines; the four curves are vertically offset and unlabelled individually.

observations.observation: The figure is a single double-logarithmic SAXS plot with y-axis 'Intensity (cm⁻¹)' and x-axis 'q (nm⁻¹)'.
Printed x-axis major tick labels are 0.1, 1 and 10 nm⁻¹, and the plotted data span approximately 0.02 to 15 nm⁻¹.
Printed y-axis tick values are -2, 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10, indicating offset logarithmic intensity values rather than absolute intensities.
The legend contains exactly five entries: Fe-5AL (open circle), Fe-6AL (open square), Fe-6.8AL (open triangle), Fe-9AL (open diamond) and a thick dark line labelled 'fits'.

Four separate curve stacks are plotted, each shifted vertically relative to the others, and none of the individual curves carries a direct composition label, so curve-to-composition assignment cannot be made from the pixels alone.
All four data sets decrease monotonically with increasing q and show a change of slope / flattening at the highest q values plotted.
Thin red broken lines with dots are overlaid on each data set in addition to the thick dark fit lines.
The caption states that open symbols are experimental data and solid lines are fitted curves obtained with Eq. (3).
The caption states that the curves have been offset vertically by a corresponding factor to avoid crowding the plot.
The caption states that the broken lines with dots are proportional to q⁻⁴.
The caption describes the figure as the variation of logarithmic SAXS intensity as a function of q for Fe-Al low-density steels with different compositions.

The paper abstract states that a composition corresponding to 6.8 wt% aluminium was studied to understand the underlying strengthening mechanisms and that microstructural features were analysed using Mössbauer spectroscopy.
No numeric intensity or q value, offset factor or fitted parameter is printed anywhere on the plot; only the axis ticks and the legend text are readable numbers/strings.

unreadable_items: the vertical offset factor applied to each individual curve is not printed
no composition label is attached to any individual curve, so which curve corresponds to which alloy is not resolvable from the pixels
at the supplied resolution it is ambiguous whether the thin red broken lines are the q⁻⁴ guides or a second fitted trace, since the caption assigns the solid lines to the fits
the exact high-q divergence between data symbols and fit lines is not quantitatively resolvable
